# TimelineItem

> One event in a Timeline: a 12px dot, a line down to the next event, what happened, when, and a sentence if it needs one.

## Install

It lands in `src/rost/timeline-item/`, with what it needs and its contract. In an app that uses shadcn:

```sh
npx shadcn add https://rost.build/r/timeline-item.json
```

Then import `src/rost/fonts.css` and `src/rost/tokens.css` once, at the root of the app. More on this in [Install](../INSTALL.md).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `current` | boolean |  | `false` |
| `last` | boolean |  | `false` |
| `title` | slot |  |  |
| `time` | slot |  |  |
| `children` | slot |  |  |

## Anatomy

- `root`: An `<li>`: the rail on the left, the words on the right, 12px apart.
- `rail`: A 12px column for the dot and the line. 4px above the dot puts it in the middle of the title's line.
- `dot`: A 12px circle. Grey for what's past, green for where things are now.
- `line`: A 1px line from 4px under the dot to the bottom of the item, where the next dot starts 4px further down.
- `content`: The title, the time and the sentence in a column, 2px apart, with 24px under them before the next event.
- `title`: Paragraph type, medium weight, the main text colour.
- `time`: Label type in the tertiary grey.
- `body` (optional): Paragraph type, a step quieter than the title.

## When to use

- **Now in green.** Mark the event that says where things stand now as current. Only one, and usually the newest.

## When not to use

- **Colour as the only signal.** The green dot means now, but the title has to say what happened. Nobody should need the colour to read it.

## Behaviour

The dot and line are drawing. The title, the time and the sentence are the content.

## Accessibility

- **Element**: `<li>`, with the time in a `<time>` element. The current one has `aria-current="step"`. The dot and line are hidden from screen readers.
- **Colour**: The past dot is 4.3:1 on the dark page, the current one 10:1. The title is 17:1, the time 7:1.
